findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connected calendars query
findings.body: The deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess. Unlike the disconnectMutation above it, it never invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. After a successful cache deletion the list item will keep showing the old cacheUpdatedAt until the query is refetched by some other action or remount, so the UI displays stale cache status immediately after the user deletes cached data.

findings.title: Delete cache fails for delegated calendar credentials shown in the UI
findings.body: The handler authorizes the request by requiring a Credential with id equal to credentialId and userId equal to the current user id. However, CredentialActionsDropdown renders the delete-cache action whenever the integration is Google Calendar and cacheUpdatedAt exists, without considering delegationCredentialId. The previous UI explicitly commented that delegation credentials cannot be disconnected by the current user, which indicates those credentials are not owned by them. For such delegated Google Calendar connections the delete action will therefore be shown but the mutation will fail with 'Credential not found or access denied'. Either hide delete for delegated credentials or add an authorization path that allows deleting the corresponding calendar cache.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds filters only by credentialId and takes the max updatedAt, but does not filter by expiresAt. getCachedAvailability only serves rows where expiresAt is at least now, so a credential with only expired cache rows will still show a 'Last updated' timestamp and a delete-cache action in the UI even though the cache is no longer used. This gives users a misleading cache status. Filter expired rows here, or otherwise treat the displayed status as valid cached data only.

findings.title: Timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The cache timestamp uses new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) regardless of the user's configured locale. Since the rest of the component uses useLocale() for translations, non-English users will see English/US date formatting. Use the active locale from useLocale or omit the explicit locale so Intl uses the user's default.
